sentences.text: Amelacanthus was an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish belonging to the elasmobranchs, a group that includes sharks and rays.
This fish is one of the few Ctenacanth species to survive the Permian-Triassic extinction event, although it died out shortly after in the Early Triassic.
Scientists know about this animal primarily through fin spines, which are rare fossil remains.
The genus was first described by Maisey in 1982.
Today, four described species are recognized within this genus.
Fossils of Amelacanthus have been found in North America, Europe, and Africa during the Carboniferous and Permian periods.
Specimens are also known from the Famennian stage in Russia.
Additional fossils were discovered in Oman from the Wordian stage of the Permian and the Induan stage of the Triassic.
